People in India are switching to UPI because it makes paying someone as easy as sending a message. You open any payments app, scan a code or type a phone number, enter your PIN, and the money moves between bank accounts in seconds. There are no cards to carry, no machines to rent and no cash to count.

It has also spread far beyond big cities. A small tea stall, a vegetable seller and a large mall can all show the same kind of QR code, so shoppers can pay almost anywhere. Because every major app works with every bank, people are not locked into one company. Friends can split a bill or send money home without worrying about which app the other person uses.

Here are the three main reasons:

Speed and ease: Payments take a few seconds, work day or night, and need only a phone and a PIN.
Low or no cost: Most everyday payments are free for the person paying, and small shops avoid card machine fees and bank trips.
Works everywhere: One QR code is accepted by every UPI app and bank, from street stalls to online stores.

Together, these make UPI the easiest choice for most daily spending.
